_pack_version_comment: Bumped only when ONNX/HEF bytes change OR a new artifact filename is introduced. Engine release workflow pulls model assets from the `models-${pack_version}` GitHub Release (cut once, reused by every engine cut). Workflow: regenerate ONNX (`gen_*.py --all-static`) -> compile HEFs (`gen_*_hailo.py`) -> bump this field -> commit -> `gh release create models-vN --prerelease ...` -> upload models there. Bumping this WITHOUT cutting the matching `models-vN` release breaks the next engine release build. v7 adds the text-to-speech voices under tts/ (uploaded to the pack release as ONE asset, `tts.tar`, which unpacks to tts/...; release.yml checks every `sherpa-onnx` artifact's sha256 after unpacking); all v6 artifacts are byte-identical. v6 (BUG-221) recompiles the yolo26n and yoloe26_s HEFs with a clamped class-branch quantisation range; ONNX and all other artifacts are byte-identical to v5. v5 (M_NATIVE_ASPECT) retired the square inputs: every detector ships the native 16:9 ladder (512x288/1024x576/1536x864) for both ONNX and Hailo-8 HEF; dinov2-s-v1 stays 224 (crop encoder). All rectangular HEFs are operator-compiled via the DFC (no public prebuilt) and ship sha256=PENDING_COMPILE + requires_compile=true until compiled. See /memories/repo/nexus-models-manifest-pending-compile.md and tools/models/README.md §'Hailo HEF compilation'.

models._comment: YOLOv26-nano on the native 16:9 ladder (512x288 / 1024x576 / 1536x864 — exact 16:9 ∩ stride-32, W=512k / H=288k; see docs/edge-core/M_NATIVE_ASPECT.md). Static shapes are mandatory for the Intel NPU plugin (silent CPU fallback on dynamic shapes) and let the OpenVINO blob cache hit on subsequent boots. Per-camera shape override picks a rung; default 512x288. Regenerate with `python tools/models/gen_yolo26n.py --all-static` before tagging a release. Detector output is NMS-baked [1,300,6]; the Hailo path cuts the graph at the six FPN head convs (raw multi-output, CPU NMS).

models._comment: DINOv2-S backbone export (Meta facebook/dinov2-small). Powers Phase 5.6 wedge identity graph: per-track 224x224 RGB crop -> 384-dim CLS-token appearance fingerprint. Apache-2.0 weights, LVD-142M curated-public-web training set (no PII targeting). Static batch=1 for NPU/OpenVINO blob-cache hits. Regenerate via `python tools/models/gen_dinov2.py`; the script patches the sha256 below in place and writes the .sha256 sidecar that the engine release workflow downloads from the models-v2 GitHub release.

artifacts._comment: M_HAILO_EP — Hailo-8 compiled artifact for dinov2_s_224 (ViT-S/14 backbone, 384-dim CLS-token output). NO public Model Zoo build; operator MUST compile via tools/models/gen_dinov2_hailo.py. Hailo-8 ViT support is partial — expect <1% top-1 drift on cosine distances vs. the FP32 ONNX path, which may require re-tuning the cloud linker `COSINE_MAX` from 0.40 if you swap to the HEF in the appearance-embedding pipeline (Phase 5.6). Calibration: 1024-image ImageNet val sample @ 224x224 RGB.

presets._comment: Only operating point. DINOv2 ViTs are trained at 224 and the engine doesn't benefit from larger crops for a per-track appearance fingerprint.

presets.name: 224-hef
presets._comment: M_HAILO_EP — Hailo-8 backed appearance embedding. Same CLS-token output (384 floats per crop); expect minor accuracy drift vs. ONNX baseline. See requires_compile.

models._comment: Files from k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx's `tts-models` release (vits-piper-en_US-ljspeech-medium.tar.bz2, sha256 3dfb4b759d8be032a4903a9538d128b0fda2a06ab1de6cbc2d93a97e2dd83dba), renamed to model.onnx / tokens.txt. The weights are Piper VITS voices from rhasspy/piper-voices (repo licence MIT); the author (Bryce Beattie, brycebeattie.com/files/tts) also releases this voice to the public domain. Trained from scratch (model card), so no lineage to the research-only Blizzard-2013 Lessac checkpoint that most Piper voices are fine-tuned from. sherpa-onnx 2.x does not phonemise Piper voices itself: nexus-tts phonemises with espeak-ng (piper-phonemize-sys) using the tts-espeak-ng-data entry.

Files from k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx's `tts-models` release (vits-piper-en_US-norman-medium.tar.bz2, sha256 1f32065d480abe9abc7c7f91442125d0b34c1cc065d1e600466cac408eabf3b8), renamed to model.onnx / tokens.txt. The weights are Piper VITS voices from rhasspy/piper-voices (repo licence MIT); the author (Bryce Beattie, brycebeattie.com/files/tts) also releases this voice to the public domain; the dataset is his own LibriVox selection. Trained from scratch (model card), so no lineage to the research-only Blizzard-2013 Lessac checkpoint that most Piper voices are fine-tuned from. sherpa-onnx 2.x does not phonemise Piper voices itself: nexus-tts phonemises with espeak-ng (piper-phonemize-sys) using the tts-espeak-ng-data entry.

Files from k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx's `tts-models` release (vits-piper-es_ES-carlfm-x_low.tar.bz2, sha256 15585c5add2ab1915ce69e8c966c7c9fb0b6afb21f9b92f18110fda5a4787f99), renamed to model.onnx / tokens.txt. The weights are Piper VITS voices from rhasspy/piper-voices (repo licence MIT); dataset github.com/carlfm01/my-speech-datasets, declared public domain. No Latin-American Spanish Piper voice passed: es_MX-ald and es_AR-daniela descend from the Lessac checkpoint, es_MX-claude has no stated dataset or lineage. Trained from scratch (model card), so no lineage to the research-only Blizzard-2013 Lessac checkpoint that most Piper voices are fine-tuned from. sherpa-onnx 2.x does not phonemise Piper voices itself: nexus-tts phonemises with espeak-ng (piper-phonemize-sys) using the tts-espeak-ng-data entry.

Not a voice (no `voice` field): the espeak-ng phoneme tables and the en/es dictionaries nexus-tts needs to turn text into phonemes, the minimum subset of the espeak-ng-data/ directory shipped in the voice archives above (phonemes checked identical to the full set). espeak-ng is GPL-3.0-or-later, on the AGENTS.md rule 1 allowlist.
